info.bio:
Beyoncé (4 de septiembre de 1981) es el nombre artístico de Beyoncé Giselle Knowles; Cantante de POP y  R&B, compositora, productora discográfica y actriz estadounidense.

Nacida y criada en Houston, Texas, se inscribió en varias escuelas de artes escénicas, y se expuso por primera vez a los concurso de canto y baile cuando era una niña. Knowles saltó a la fama a finales de los 90 como la cantante principal del grupo Destiny's Child, el cual ha vendido más de 50 millones de discos en todo el mundo.

podcast.title: Album of the Year Loss to Beck (2015)
podcast.body: Beyoncé's universally acclaimed fifth album, "Beyoncé," lost the Album of the Year Grammy to Beck's "Morning Phase" in 2015, an event that sparked an uproar, including Kanye West's brief stage interruption. This was the first of three consecutive Album of the Year nominations for Beyoncé that did not result in a win. "Beyoncé's game-changing self-title 2013 album, one that, as we discussed in a prior hit parade episode, had invented the surprise album drop, lost the album of the year Grammy to Beck."

podcast.title: Zero for Eight at 2018 Grammys
podcast.body: Jay-Z, Beyoncé's husband, went "zero for eight" at the 2018 Grammys, despite the couple having a combined 56 Grammys (32 for her, 24 for him) plus one for their daughter Blue Ivy Carter. This illustrates the point about their lack of success in general field categories. "just after Jay had gone zero for eight at that year's Grammys."

podcast.title: 2023 Tour High Ticket & Service Charges
podcast.body: For Beyoncé's 2023 tour, some tickets were sold for as much as $4,000. Due to service charges being set as a percentage of the face value, the service charge on these high-priced tickets could reach up to $550, illustrating the significant impact of percentage-based fees on expensive tickets. "If we look at Beyonce's 2023 tour, some tickets sold for $4,000 and the service charge, a percentage of the face value, could be as high as $550."

podcast.title: Most Grammys Won by a Single Artist
podcast.body: As of the podcast episode, Beyoncé holds the record for most Grammys ever won by a single artist, with 32 awards. However, almost none of these prizes were won in the general field categories, which is considered "rather unjust" given her critical and commercial success. podcast.title: Overlooked in Top Categories
podcast.body: Beyoncé is consistently overlooked in the top general field Grammy categories, despite being a "superlative R&B singer." This is attributed to her "proximity to rap and hip hop culture," which the Academy historically struggles to fully embrace in major awards. "Beyoncé, I would venture, has been overlooked in the top categories, even as a superlative, R&B singer for her proximity to rap and hip hop culture."

xref.title: Unique Sound in 2009 Musical Landscape
xref.body: In 2009, Mumford & Sons' English folk sound, featuring accordions, banjos, and ukuleles, was considered "a million miles away from what anyone else was offering," providing a stark contrast to the dominant alt-rock bands and pop stars like Beyonce, Katy Perry, and Justin Bieber. "What Mumford was offering the world in 2009 was a million miles away from what anyone else was offering."

xref.title: Assorted Controversial Actions
xref.body: Al Jourgensen has a long history of controversial and confrontational behaviors, including stealing drugs from Courtney Love, physically assaulting R. Kelly for an action that distressed Jourgensen's daughter, and attacking Metallica with vegetables. He also insisted that Limp Bizkit frontman Fred Durst wear nothing but a cowboy hat during a vocal session he produced, blew up Ministry's tour bus with a large firework purchased from a homeless person, and was ejected from the Grammy Awards for screaming at Beyoncé. "Al Jorgensen stole drugs from Courtney Love. He punched out our kelly for doing something that freaked out his daughter. He attacked Metallica with some vegetables."
